 :JUDGMENT:
This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioner against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.15,00,000/ for the injuries sustained in the Road Traffic accident.
2.

The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 15092022 at about 7.00 a.m., the Petitioner was crossing the road near Mallathalli bus stand, outer ring road, Bangalore.
At that time, a motor cycle bearing No.KA01JL 9141 ridden by its rider in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against petitioner.
Due to the impact, the Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately after the accident, the Petitioner was shifted to Abaya hospital and thereafter he was shifted to BGS Global hospital, wherein he was admitted as an inpatient.
3. Prior to the accident, the Petitioner was hale and healthy and he was working as security guard and was earning Rs.20,000/ per month.
Due to the accident, he has sustained grievous injuries causing permanent disablement.

4. The Respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending motor cycle and therefore, Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the Petitioner.
Hence, this Petition.
5. In pursuance of service of notice, the Respondent No.1 though appeared before the court through his counsel but not filed objection statement.
Respondent No.2 appeared before the court through it's counsel and filed objections to the main petition.

In the Objection Statement of Respondent No.2, it denied the age, avocation and income of the Petitioner and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of motor cycle by its rider.
Further it has denied the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in the accident and the expenses incurred for the medical treatment.
Further it admitted the issuance of policy in respect of motor cycle in favour of 1st respondent.
It is further contended that the accident was not caused due to rash and negligent riding of offending vehicle by its rider.
Further contended that the accident occurred due to negligence of petitioner himself.
Further contended that the rider of motor cycle was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident.

The respondent No.1 knowing fully well entrusted the vehicle to a person who did not possess valid and effective Prabhulingaiah K.M vs Ramesha M.R on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16308909/
2 driving licence to ride the same on the date of accident.

Hence, among these and other grounds,
Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
6. On the basis of the above pleadings, my learned predecessor has framed the following Issues.
ISSUES 1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that he had sustained grievous injuries in a Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 1509 2022 at about 7.00 a.m., near Malathahalli bus stand, Old outer ring road,
Mallathahalli, Bangalore, due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA01JL9141?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?
3. What Order or Award?
7. In order to substantiate the case of the Petitioner, the Petitioner got examined himself as P.W.1 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to P14.
He also examined a doctor as PW.2 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.15 and 16 and closed his side evidence.

PW.1 and 2 tendered for cross examination done at length by the learned advocate for respondent No.2.
8.
On the other hand, to rebut the evidence of petitioner respondent No.2 has not adduced any oral or documentary evidence.
9. The documents got marked through PW.1 and 2

are - The certified copy of FIR at Ex.P.1, certified copy of complaint at Ex.P.2, certified copy of spot mahazar at Ex.P.3, certified copy of spot sketch at Ex. P.4, certified copy of IMV report at Ex.P.5, certified copy of wound certificate at Ex.P.6,
Discharge summary at Ex.P.7, certified copy of MLC extract at Ex.P.8, certified copy of notice issued u/s 133 of MV Act at Ex.P.9, certified copy of Reply in respect of Ex.P.9 is marked at Ex. P.10,,
certified copy of charge sheet at Ex.P.11, Medical bills at Ex.P.12, Xray at Ex. P.13, notarised copy of Aadhar card of PW.1 at Ex. P.14, Clinical assessment proforma and calculation sheet at Ex. P.15 and Xrays with report at Ex. P.16.

10. Having heard the arguments of the learned Counsel for the Petitioner and the learned Counsel for the Respondent No.2, upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
 Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative  Issue No. 2 : Partly in the Affirmative  Issue No. 3 : As per the Final Order  for the following :

sentences.text: Issue No. 1 : It is the case of the Petitioner that he had sustained grievous injuries in the Road Traffic accident that occurred on 15092022 at about 7.00 a.m. due to the rash and negligent riding of the motor cycle bearing Regn.No.KA01JL9141 by its rider.
12. On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 has denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the motor cycle bearing Regn.No.KA01JL9141 by its rider.
13. In order to prove the case of the Petitioner, he got examined himself as P.W.1 and he also examined doctor as PW.2 and got marked documents as per Ex.P.1 to Ex.P16 as noted above.
14. P.W.1 has reiterated the Petition averments in his chiefaffidavit.

Upon careful consideration of the documents, Ex.P1 and 2 i.e., Certified copies of FIR and Complaint which shows that on the Complaint lodged, the SHO of Kamakshipalya Traffic police station registered the case against the rider of the motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA01JL9141 for the offences punishable under Sections 279, 338 of IPC.
The documents Ex.P.3 to 5 and Ex. P.9 to 11 would justify the fact that there is involvement of No.KA01JL9141 vehicle in the accident.
15. The document Ex.P.5 shows that the accident was not due to any mechanical defects.
The document Ex.P.6 justify the fact that the petitioner has sustained grievous and simple injuries.

The document Ex.P.11 justify the fact that after thorough investigation the IO has submitted charge sheet against the rider of motor cycle arraying him as accused for the offences punishable u/s 279, 338 of IPC.
16.
The further document Ex.P.7 justify the fact that the petitioner took treatment at BGS Global hospital as an inpatient from 15092022 to 29092022.
The document I.e., discharge summary of BGS Global hospital would discloses the fact that petitioner took treatment as an inpatient.
Ex.P.12 justify the fact that in respect of treatments which the petitioner has taken, he has incurred medical expenses to the tune of Rs.1,18,503/.
The documents Ex. P.9 and 10 justify the fact that as on the date of accident, the offending vehicle in question was ridden by Ramesha.M.R. S/o Ramaiah who is none other than the accused in Ex. P.11.
Ex. P.10 would further justify the fact that the said rider had valid and effective driving licence to ride the vehicle and that the vehicle in question had valid insurance policy as on that date.
17. During his examination in chief, PW.1 has reiterated the averments made in the petition.
Though PW.1 has been subjected to cross examination at length, nothing worth to discredit the case of the petitioner has been elicited from his mouth.
Such being the case, it is clear that the petitioner/PW.1 has withstood his case even during his cross examination.
There are suggestions made to PW.1 denying the fact of him incurring expenses to the tune of Rs.1,18,503/ for medical expenses.
Such suggestions have been denied by PW.1.
Moreover, the medical bills are not seriously disputed during the course of cross examination.
18. It is pertinent to note that according to the petitioner, prior to the incident he was working as security guard and was earning Rs.20,000/p.m.
Admittedly, no supportive documents have been furnished by the petitioner to prove his avocation and his monthly income.

Having considered the Prabhulingaiah K.M vs Ramesha M.R on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16308909/
4 date of occurrence of accident, in the light of the guidelines of Karnataka Legal Services authority,
the notional income of the petitioner should be taken as Rs.15,500/p.m. for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
19. According to the petitioner he was 50 years old when the incident occurred.
The respondent No.2 has denied the age of petitioner.
In order to substantiate his age, the petitioner has produced his Aadhar card at Ex.
As per Aadhar card, the date of birth of the petitioner is shown as 17.12.1971.
Accident has taken place on 15.09.2022.
Hence, the age of the petitioner is taken as 51 years, same may be considered and accordingly same is considered.

20. The allegations made by the petitioner that the accident occurred as a result of negligence and rashness on the part of the rider of offending vehicle has been denied by the respondent No.2 in its statement of objections.
Several suggestions have also been made during the course of cross examination of PW.1 which were categorically denied by PW.1.
The oral evidence given by PW.1 corroborates the documentary evidence.

The over all consideration of the evidence of petitioner, it is clear that the petitioner has been able to prove the fact that as a result of rash and negligent on the part of rider of motor cycle bearing No.KA01JL9141 accident occurred and and as a result of said accident, the petitioner sustained injuries.

Hence, issue No.1 is answered in the 'Affirmative'.
21. Issue No. 2 :
As the petitioner has proved that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the offending motor cycle by its rider, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation.
22. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioner is entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I COMPENSATION TOWARDS PAIN, SHOCK AND SUFFERING:
23.

The Wound Certificate i.e., Ex.P6 and other medical records reveals that in the accident the Petitioner has sustained following injuries:
1. Swelling and tenderness present over left leg middle 1/3rd, abnormal mobility present.
2. Abrasion present over left forearm above the wrist joint.
As per the opinion of the doctor, the injury No.1 is grievous in nature and injury No.2 is simple in nature.

Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that,
awarding compensation of Rs.25,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

II COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF AMENITIES:
24.
Bearing in mind the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.25,000/ under this head would be just and reasonable.

Prabhulingaiah K.M vs Ramesha M.R on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16308909/
5 III COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF INCOME DURING THE LAID -UP PERIOD:
25.
The Petitioner has averred in the petition as well as in his evidence that he was admitted in BGS Global hospital as an inpatient from 15092022 to 29092022.
The document I.e., discharge summary of BGS Global hospital would disclose the fact that petitioner took treatment as an inpatient.
Further, P.W.2 has also reiterated the same in his evidence.
Therefore, the total period which the petitioner was admitted as an inpatient is 15 days.
26. Having regard to the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, I am of the opinion that the laid up period may be considered as two months.
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.31,000/ under this head (@ Rs.15,500/ per month).

IV COMPENSATION TOWARDS ATTENDANT'S CHARGES, EXTRA DIET & NOURISHMENT AND CONVEYANCE :
27.

Admittedly, the Petitioner has sustained injuries and during the laid up period, the Petitioner might have engaged an attendant and also he might have spent some amount towards extra diet and nourishment and for his conveyance.

In the facts and circumstances of the case, awarding compensation of Rs.5,000/ towards attendants charges, Rs.5,000/ towards extra diet and nourishment and Rs.5,000/ towards conveyance would be just and reasonable.
In all, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,000/ under this head.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS MEDICAL EXPENCES :
28. The Petitioner has deposed that he has spent around Rs.5,00,000/ towards medical expenses and other expenses.
In order to prove this fact, he has produced 53 medical bills i.e., Ex.P.12 which is totally amounting to Rs.1,18,503/.
There is no serious dispute regarding the medical bills.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.1,18,503/ which is rounded off to Rs.1,18,503/ as a compensation under this head.
VI COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF FUTURE EARNINGS/COMPENSATION TOWARDS PERMANENT DISABILITY :

29 . The Petitioner has alleged that due to the injuries sustained by him in the accident, he is not able to walk for long distance, stand, sit for long duration, climb or descend stairs, cannot stand firmly,
limp while walking, there is restriction of movements in his leg, cannot stand firmly, there are ugly looking operative scars over his legs, cannot sleep comfortably due to pain, finding difficulty carry out his day to day routine activities.
P.W.1 has deposed to that effect.
30. Further, the Petitioner got examined doctor by name Dr.Rajesh.M.B as P.W.2 who also deposed regarding the injuries sustained by the petitioner in a road traffic accident and examination he made.
Further, he got marked Clinical assessment proforma and calculation sheet and Xray with report at Ex.P.15 and 16.
He assessed disability permanent physical disability to the left lower limb at 43%.

Prabhulingaiah K.M vs Ramesha M.R on 10 April, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/16308909/
6 31.
In the crossexamination PW.2 has admitted that he has not treated the petitioner.
He has admitted that he has examined the petitioner only during the assessment of disability and fracture is united with implants in situ.
There is no limb shortening.
There is no loss of bone, there is no loss of muscle but there is loss of muscle power.
He has also admitted that range of movements of left hip is normal and there are restrictions of movements of left ankle and left knee.
He has denied the suggestion that to help the petitioner he has assessed the disability at 43%.

Hence, having regard to the medical records placed on hand and the nature of the injuries sustained by the Petitioner and by considering the nature of his work, I am of the opinion that considering the disability of the Petitioner with respect to the whole body at 8% would be just and proper.
As per Sarla Verma's Case (2009 ACJ 1298 SC), the multiplier applicable to the Petitioner is 11.

With multiplier of 11, income of Rs.15,500/ per month and disability of the Petitioner with respect to his whole body at 8%, the loss of future income comes to Rs.1,63,680/ (Rs.15,500/ x 12 = 1,86,000/
, Rs.1,86,000/x 11 x 8/100 = 1,63,680/).
Hence, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.1,63,680/ under this head.

TOTAL COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONER IS ENTITLED:
32.

To sum up, the Petitioner is entitled for compensation under the following heads :
1. Pain, shock & Suffering Rs. 25,000/
2. Loss of amenities Rs. 25,000/
3. Attendant's charges, Extra Rs. 15,000/ diet, and conveyance 4.

Medical expenses Rs. 1,18,503/
5. Loss of income during the Rs. 31,000/ laid up period 6.
Loss of Future income Rs.1,63,680/ Total Rs.3,78,183/

Thus, totally the Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.3,78,183/ which is rounded off to Rs.3,78,200/ with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of this petition till the date of realization.

33. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent riding on the part of the rider of the offending vehicle bearing No.KA01 JL9141.
The Petition shows the Policy is valid and in force at the time of accident.
There is no dispute about the validity of the policy.
Therefore, Respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioner.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "Partly in the Affirmative".
34. ISSUE No. 3 :

In view of my findings on Issue No.1 and 2, I proceed to pass the following:
